routes.title: Test an AI data-protection gate inside BPOM's compliance rollout
routes.impactRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.actor: Badan POM (BPOM), acting as public-body data controller; external enforcement institution remains to be verified.
routes.obligor: BPOM for an identified high-risk personal-data processing operation; no actual AI deployment or supplier has yet been identified.
routes.instrument: Law 27/2022 Article 34 requires impact assessment for high-risk processing, including significant automated decisions and new technology. BPOM's September 2026 compliance programme supplies a concrete implementation setting.
routes.safeguard: Proposed: select one AI-assisted complaints or clinical-data workflow; require a signed assessment, personal-data leakage tests, human review and documented mitigation before production access.
routes.verification: Proposed: retain versioned test cases, access logs, a signed go/no-go record and a retest after mitigation; demonstrate whether a failed case actually blocks deployment.
routes.remedy: Proposed internal hold on the selected deployment. Article 57 lists administrative sanctions, including suspension of processing; the competent operational enforcer and procedure need verification before claiming an external veto.
routes.window: Actual event: BPOM compliance workshop, 15 September 2026, following reported promulgation of PP 33/2026 on 16 July 2026. BPOM announced follow-up assessment and processing records. No dated tender, preparation-period end or 2027 pilot slot verified. Proposed validation by 21–22 June 2027 is a project target, not an official deadline.
routes.evidenceSummary: A statutory assessment instrument and a named public-body implementation programme are evidenced. Neither a completed BPOM AI assessment nor adoption of the proposed gate was found.
routes.gap: Full PP 33/2026 text and current establishment/delegation of the supervisory institution remain unverified; no system inventory, procurement contract or pilot approval.
routes.nextQuestion: Which BPOM processing operation is both AI-enabled and subject to Article 34, and who can sign and enforce its pre-production hold?
incentives: Proposed benefit: turn compliance preparation into a demonstrable operational control.
Proposed benefit: reuse one assessment dossier across privacy and deployment decisions.
constraints: Privacy assessment does not establish a general frontier-model release power.
A supplier may control evidence that BPOM cannot obtain under existing terms.
External enforcement readiness cannot be inferred from a ministerial announcement.

routes.title: Attach evidence of AI risk mitigation to a Malaysian commercial DPIA
routes.impactRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.actor: A participating Malaysian commercial data controller, using the Personal Data Protection Commissioner's assessment guideline.
routes.obligor: The selected commercial controller; a contracted processor only to the extent required by applicable terms. Federal and state governments are exempt from Act 709.
routes.instrument: 2026 DPIA Guideline, sections 6–10 and Annex A: high-risk screening, assessment and senior-management consideration, including AI examples. This is not a general government AI procurement mandate.
routes.safeguard: Proposed: append reproducible privacy-leakage and harmful automated-decision tests to one AI assessment; contract for evidence access and make unresolved critical findings a production hold.
routes.verification: Proposed: freeze a synthetic test set and system version, record baseline failures and retest fixes; inspect the signed management decision and whether the hold was exercised.
routes.remedy: Proposed contractual/internal hold and corrective retest. The guideline permits management to accept residual risk; a regulator-imposed AI launch veto is not established here.
routes.window: Existing 2026 guideline provides an implementation route. Official consultation portal lists the separate AI/privacy framework consultation as 5–24 October 2026, closed. A specific 2027 adoption date or pilot intake was not verified. Seek a deployment-linked pilot before the project checkpoint of 21–22 June 2027, not a purported reopened consultation.
routes.evidenceSummary: Published guidance provides a practical assessment instrument; the separate AI framework is a consultation, not established adoption. No participating controller or executed gate has been identified.
routes.gap: Need the controller, system scope, processor evidence terms and written no-go criteria. Exact guideline release day and any final AI-framework publication remain unverified.
routes.nextQuestion: Will a commercial controller choose a 2027 AI rollout and give its assessment an enforceable, testable critical-failure hold?
incentives: Proposed benefit: use one evidence package for privacy assurance and vendor acceptance.
Proposed benefit: discover costly deployment defects before real customer exposure.
constraints: Government exemption prevents treating the country's entire public sector as covered.
Management risk acceptance can weaken the proposed gate.
Privacy scope excludes many advanced-AI harms and does not control upstream model release.

routes.title: Turn a Thai AI Governance Sandbox test into a deployment decision
routes.impactRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.actor: Electronic Transactions Development Agency (ETDA), through its internal AI Governance Practice Center, with a participating use-case owner.
routes.obligor: Prospective sandbox participant under pilot terms still to be agreed; no statutory deployment veto established.
routes.instrument: ETDA's announced 2027 AI Governance Sandbox: controlled evaluation of real use cases before wider deployment. A signed participant gate would be a new instrument, not an existing statutory condition.
routes.safeguard: Proposed: one domestic public-service chatbot pilot with a preregistered harmful-output/privacy evaluation and a critical-failure threshold linked to the owner's production decision.
routes.verification: Proposed: independent rerun of held-out Thai-language cases, versioned failure records, remediation and one observed go/no-go decision. Use synthetic scenarios and document scope limitations.
routes.remedy: Proposed participant agreement to withhold wider rollout until critical failures are fixed. ETDA authority to compel this outside the agreement is unverified.
routes.window: 5 October 2026 announcement identifies 2027 programme direction. No application deadline, admitted cohort or pre-June completion slot verified. 21–22 June 2027 is the project's validation checkpoint; sandbox participation and scheduling must be confirmed first.
routes.evidenceSummary: An official operational sandbox proposal exists beyond a national strategy. ETDA describes prior ethical-LLM work, but no binding admission rules or participant-specific decision record was retrieved.
routes.gap: Missing intake rules, participant identity, committed evaluator time, evidence access and contractual deployment hold.
routes.nextQuestion: Can ETDA identify a 2027 domestic sandbox case whose owner will bind production deployment to a published critical-failure test before June?
incentives: Proposed benefit: give the sandbox an observable decision outcome rather than only a workshop output.
Proposed benefit: let a participant discover local-language failures before expanding deployment.
constraints: Voluntary participation is not nationwide coverage.
Evaluation capacity and developer cooperation may constrain timing.
International prompt collaboration is separate from this national pilot and is not assumed necessary.

routes.title: Test a public-service AI impact assessment at the approval point
routes.impactRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.actor: Head of the deploying Vietnamese state agency; Ministry of Science and Technology (MOST) oversees assessment implementation.
routes.obligor: A selected state agency deploying AI within Article 20's scope; no particular agency or supplier has yet agreed a pilot.
routes.instrument: Decree 142/2026/ND-CP, Article 20 and Form AI02: assessment for high-risk state-agency systems or specified rights/public-interest systems whose results directly ground administrative decisions. Agency-head approval precedes use.
routes.safeguard: Proposed: attach reproducible harmful-decision, leakage and human-intervention tests to one public-service AI assessment, and use unresolved critical failures as explicit approval-withholding criteria.
routes.verification: Proposed: inspect the approved dossier and a versioned baseline/retest comparison; run an intervention exercise showing a human can override the system and prevent a harmful decision.
routes.remedy: Proposed exercise of the agency's pre-use approval point to withhold deployment pending mitigation. No general upstream-model ban or automatic penalty for this proposed test threshold is claimed.
routes.window: Decree issued 30 April 2026 and effective 1 May 2026. The opportunity is a qualifying deployment or material change, not an identified 2027 consultation. No agency rollout date verified. Select a qualifying case and test before the project checkpoint of 21–22 June 2027; this target is not prescribed by the decree.
routes.evidenceSummary: Article 20 assigns agency-head approval, assessment updating and MOST oversight. The legal assessment is established; the proposed critical-failure test and a participating implementation are not.
routes.gap: Need a named system, confirmation of scope, a deployment date, signatory and access to a publishable dossier. Supplier evidence rights and assessment practice are unknown.
routes.nextQuestion: Which agency has a qualifying AI deployment before June 2027 and will show that its assessment can actually withhold approval?
incentives: Proposed benefit: turn an assessment form into evidence that the approval control operates.
Proposed benefit: reuse a documented human-intervention test for operational readiness.
constraints: The legal duty does not demonstrate implementation quality or actual refusal of approval.
Disclosure exceptions may limit independent verification.
Public-service scope cannot be extrapolated to national AI compute or GDP.
